quiz.q: Inputs total 0.15 bitcoin and outputs total 0.1499 bitcoin. What is the difference?
options: The transaction fee, collected by the miner
rationales: Bitcoin amounts are exact integers of satoshis; nothing is rounded away.
Change is itself an output, so it is already counted in the 0.1499.

quiz.q: Alice pays 5 bitcoins using a 20-bitcoin input. Ignoring the fee, what is the change?
rationales: The whole input is spent; 20 would mean the store got nothing.
5 is the payment to the store, not the change.

quiz.q: When does a transaction become part of the blockchain?
options: When a miner includes it in a block that full nodes validate
As soon as the wallet signs it
When a block explorer shows it
rationales: Signing makes it valid to relay; it is not yet in any block.
Explorers display what they see, including unconfirmed transactions.

quiz.q: By the whitepaper, an attacker with 10% of the hash power catches up from six blocks behind with probability about:
rationales: 0.2 is the probability at one confirmation, not six.
0.05 is roughly the probability at two confirmations.

quiz.q: In PROV-O terms, what is a Bitcoin transaction in a chain of spends?
options: An activity that derives new outputs from earlier ones
rationales: The agent is the key holder who signs; the transaction is what happens.
Nothing about a transaction chain is a document on the web.
